quick: Use only if clearly needed (limited data)
Increase dosing interval (CrCl-based); adjust after dialysis
No dose adjustment for impairment per se
HBV DNA, CK (myopathy), LFTs; lactic acidosis signs
summary: Telbivudine is an oral synthetic thymidine nucleoside analogue used to treat chronic hepatitis B in adults with evidence of viral replication and active disease. It is given as 600 mg once daily and suppresses HBV DNA polymerase (reverse transcriptase). It carries a BOXED WARNING for lactic acidosis and severe hepatomegaly with steatosis (a class effect of nucleoside analogues) and for severe acute exacerbation of hepatitis on discontinuation. It is associated with myopathy (raised creatine kinase) and rare peripheral neuropathy. High rates of resistance limit its use, and it has been discontinued from the US market; this record reflects the former US label, EMA/SmPC and BNF.
indications: Treatment of chronic hepatitis B in adults with evidence of viral replication and either persistently elevated transaminases or histologically active disease

dosage.c: Adult chronic hepatitis B (normal renal function)
Renal impairment CrCl <30 mL/min (not on dialysis)

dosage.d: 600 mg once every 96 hours, administered after the haemodialysis session on dialysis days

admin: Take orally once daily, with or without food
Do not stop abruptly without medical advice - hepatitis may flare on discontinuation
Adjust the dosing interval (not the dose amount) for renal impairment
On dialysis days, take the dose after the dialysis session
Avoid combining with pegylated interferon alfa (increased peripheral neuropathy risk)
moa: Telbivudine is phosphorylated intracellularly to telbivudine 5'-triphosphate, which competes with the natural substrate thymidine 5'-triphosphate and inhibits HBV DNA polymerase (reverse transcriptase). Its incorporation into viral DNA causes chain termination, suppressing hepatitis B virus replication. It is specific for HBV and does not meaningfully inhibit human or HIV polymerases at therapeutic levels.

absolute: Combination with pegylated interferon alfa-2a (increased risk of peripheral neuropathy)
relative: Risk factors for lactic acidosis / hepatic steatosis (obesity, prolonged nucleoside exposure)
Co-administration with other agents causing myopathy
monitor: Liver function tests; signs of lactic acidosis/hepatomegaly

preg: There are limited human data; use during pregnancy only if clearly needed and the benefit outweighs the risk. An antiretroviral/HBV pregnancy registry exists for nucleoside analogues; lactic acidosis has been reported in pregnant women using nucleoside analogues.
lact: Breastfeeding is not recommended. It is excreted in milk in animals, and because of the potential for serious adverse reactions including lactic acidosis in the infant, mothers should not breastfeed while taking telbivudine.
renal: Telbivudine is renally cleared. No change in the 600 mg amount is needed, but the dosing INTERVAL must be lengthened according to creatinine clearance (every 48 h for 30-49 mL/min, every 72 h for <30 mL/min off dialysis, every 96 h after dialysis in ESRD).
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required for hepatic impairment itself, as telbivudine is not hepatically metabolised. Severe acute exacerbations of hepatitis B can occur if treatment is stopped, so monitor hepatic function for several months after discontinuation.

major: Pegylated interferon alfa - contraindicated combination; markedly increased risk of peripheral neuropathy
Other drugs associated with myopathy/rhabdomyolysis (e.g. statins, fibrates, corticosteroids) - additive muscle toxicity
moderate: Drugs that impair renal function or compete for tubular secretion - may raise telbivudine levels
Other nucleoside/nucleotide analogues - additive mitochondrial toxicity (lactic acidosis)
minor: Generally low metabolic interaction potential (not a CYP substrate/inhibitor)
interactions.food: Food does not significantly affect absorption; may be taken with or without meals.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid heavy alcohol use, which adds to the risk of hepatic injury and may compound lactic acidosis.
interactions.diagnostics: Can increase creatine kinase and transaminases; monitor HBV DNA for virological response and lactate if acidosis is suspected.

serious: Myopathy/myositis (muscle pain and weakness with elevated CK)
Severe acute exacerbation of hepatitis B on stopping treatment
emergency: Lactic acidosis (deep/rapid breathing, severe nausea, marked fatigue, muscle aches)

monitoring: HBV DNA periodically to confirm suppression and detect resistance
Creatine kinase and any muscle symptoms
Liver function tests during therapy and for months after stopping
Renal function to maintain correct dosing interval
Clinical and laboratory signs of lactic acidosis
counsel: Take one tablet at the same time each day; do not stop without speaking to your doctor as your hepatitis can flare
Report new or unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness promptly
Seek urgent care for rapid breathing, severe tiredness, stomach pain with nausea/vomiting, or dark urine
Tell your doctor about all other medicines, especially interferon and cholesterol drugs
Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine
pk: HBV DNA decline within weeks of starting therapy
Plasma peak about 1-4 hours after an oral dose
Intracellular triphosphate half-life is long; plasma elimination half-life ~40-49 hours
Once-daily dosing maintains suppression; effect wanes after stopping (risk of flare)
Store tablets at room temperature in the original container
pearls: BOXED WARNING: lactic acidosis and severe hepatomegaly with steatosis (nucleoside-analogue class effect), and severe acute hepatitis B exacerbation on discontinuation
Distinctive toxicities are myopathy (monitor CK) and, with interferon, peripheral neuropathy - the interferon combination is contraindicated
Adjust the dosing INTERVAL, not the dose amount, for renal impairment; give after dialysis
High rate of resistance and superseded by entecavir/tenofovir; telbivudine has been discontinued in the US
Monitor liver function for several months after stopping because hepatitis can flare
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as it is remembered, then resume the usual schedule; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and do not double up. Maintain the prescribed renal dosing interval.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. In overdose, stop the drug and give supportive care with monitoring for lactic acidosis, myopathy and hepatic effects; haemodialysis can remove a fraction of the drug. Manage symptomatically.
